breakdown.title: How this Build Plan is calculated
breakdown.intro: Live {{hub}} prices and this plan's own inputs. Every number below is the one the plan is using now.
breakdown.pricesMaterialsSell: Materials: {{hub}} lowest sell — what you pay to buy them now.
breakdown.pricesMaterialsBuy: Materials: {{hub}} highest buy — what they cost if you place orders and wait.
breakdown.pricesOre: Ore, ice and gas: priced as themselves. Refining is not modelled, so a plan that eats minerals prices minerals.
breakdown.pricesOwned: Owned units: 0 ISK. Ore you mined is free here — the plan does not charge what you could have sold it for.
breakdown.pricesBuilt: Built materials: their own recipe instead of a price — inputs plus job fee, at every level you chose to build.
breakdown.pricesProduct: {{product}}: always {{hub}} lowest sell, whichever side the materials use.
breakdown.materials: Quantity after ME {{me}} waste (rounded once per job, not per run) × unit price. Owned units come off first.
breakdown.materialsReaction: Quantity × unit price. Reactions have no ME, so no waste is saved. Owned units come off first.
breakdown.jobFee: EIV is CCP's reference value for the materials at ME 0 — a yardstick, not what you pay. {{system}}'s index ({{index}}) scales it, SCC adds 4%, the structure owner adds tax.
breakdown.jobFeeFormula: EIV {{eiv}} → cost index fee {{costIndexFee}} + SCC 4% {{scc}} + facility tax {{facilityTax}} = {{total}}
breakdown.revenueTitle: Revenue, sales tax and broker fee
breakdown.revenueAssumption: Assumes it fills at today's lowest sell. Undercutting, price moves and time on the market are not modelled.
breakdown.fees: From your skills: Accounting {{accounting}} sets sales tax, Broker Relations {{broker}} sets broker fee. Standings toward the station owner: {{factionStanding}} faction, {{corpStanding}} corp.
breakdown.profitNet: Net = revenue − sales tax − broker fee − total cost. The default.
breakdown.profitGross: Gross = revenue − total cost. Ignores both market fees — only realistic if you never list it.
breakdown.profitIskPerHour: ISK/hour = profit ÷ build time ({{time}}). Slot time, not time to sell.
breakdown.breakEven: What one unit must list at to cover the whole job. Fees come out of the listed price, so it sits above cost per unit.
breakdown.breakEvenFloor: Broker fee has a 100 ISK per-order minimum. Under that, 100 ISK is used and the price re-solved.
breakdown.verdictAcquisition: Acquisition: is building {{product}} cheaper than buying it? Nothing is sold, so no tax and no broker fee.
breakdown.verdictSale: Sale profitability: does building then selling make money? That one pays both fees. Same hub price, different question.
breakdown.useOrSellBody: Owned units cost the plan nothing, so the profit above is what you make on top of stock you already hold. Build if that beats what the materials would fetch, sell if it does not.
breakdown.useOrSellBases: Sell now: fills standing buy orders — paid at once, sales tax only. Sell order: lists at the hub's sell price — more ISK, but broker fee (100 ISK minimum) and you wait.
breakdown.useOrSellUnpriced: No order on the chosen side means no verdict, rather than a total that quietly drops it.
breakdown.useOrSellScope: Only the owned units this job eats are valued. Surplus is out of scope, and a material set to Built counts as itself, not as the stock behind its recipe.

useOrSell.label: Use or sell your materials?
useOrSell.intro: You already own some of what this job eats. This compares building with those units against selling them and building nothing. Only the units this job would consume are counted — stock beyond what it needs is not valued here.

useOrSell.sellNetTooltip: What your owned units fetch after fees: Sell now fills the hub's buy orders (sales tax only), Sell order lists them and waits (sales tax plus broker fee, 100 ISK minimum per stack). Click for the full breakdown.
useOrSell.verdictBuild: BUILD — using your materials beats selling them by {{amount}} ISK
useOrSell.verdictSell: SELL — selling your materials beats building by {{amount}} ISK

useOrSell.buildProfitTooltip: Always net of sales tax and broker fee, whatever the Gross/Net toggle above says: selling your materials pays those fees too, so both sides are compared after fees.

login.permissionsHint: Signing in lets it read your skills and training queue, wallet, assets, blueprints, industry jobs, mining ledger, market orders, contracts, mail, calendar, contacts, standings, clones and implants, planetary colonies, loyalty points, notifications, current location, corporation roles, your in-game fittings, and the player structures you can dock at — both their names and a search across them, which is how a build location is picked. EVE's consent screen lists the planetary scope as "manage your planetary installations" — Neocom Desk only reads that data and never writes to it. Corporation data and player-structure markets are separate grants, requested only if you open the pages that need them. Log in again after an update to pick up newly requested permissions. Want to share less from the start? Use Log in with custom permissions, next to the Log in button, to choose exactly what you grant.
login.writeExceptions: It also asks for four permissions that write, and uses each only when you act: opening a mail in this app also marks it read in EVE, so it won't show as unread again after a refresh; responding Accept, Decline, or Tentative to a calendar invite here also sends that response to EVE; replying to or forwarding a mail you write here sends it through your EVE account, the same as sending it from the game client; and saving a Fitting to EVE creates or replaces your in-game fitting there, the same as fitting it in the client. Nothing else in the app writes to EVE.
login.eyebrow: Free · Open source · Runs in your browser
login.heading: Answers, not API dumps.
login.answersHeading: The questions it exists to answer
login.answersLead: Each of these is a page you open after signing in, with the number you would have worked out by hand already worked out.

attention.question: Which character needs my attention?
attention.answer: The character list shows every pilot’s training queue at a glance: training, paused, ending soon or sitting idle. Alerts gathers what fired for every character on this device, not just the one you are looking at: skills finished, jobs ready to deliver, colonies stopped, orders undercut, mail waiting. Open a character and its board leads with the nearest deadline.

orders.question: Which of my orders is quietly losing ISK?
orders.answer: Open Orders is a worklist, not a list. Every order is filed under the worst thing wrong with it — undercut at your station, system or region, sitting under the price where relisting stops paying, or about to expire — worst first, across every character you fly. Open one and it prices the ways out: hold, undercut the station, dump into a standing buy order, or reprocess it and sell the materials, each net of the fee that exit actually pays, plus the trade hubs bidding more and how many jumps away they are.

build.question: Is this blueprint worth building today?
build.answer: A Build Plan costs the materials, job fee and taxes at live hub prices and answers two different questions instead of blurring them: is it cheaper than buying outright, and does it still profit once sales tax and broker fees come off. Sub-builds recurse into the same plan, owned stock is checked against what it would fetch if you sold it instead, and every figure on screen opens the rule it came from with your own values substituted in.

training.question: What is this training plan really going to cost me?
training.answer: Drag skills into a plan and it schedules against the character’s real attributes, implants and queue. The optimizer places remaps for you — or at markers you drop yourself — and re-costs the plan under what-if implants and an accelerator before you spend anything. Put your characters side by side to see which of them should be training it.

colonies.question: Are my colonies earning what they could?
colonies.answer: The PI Advisor reads every colony and lists what is not working — idle facilities, storage that fills before you are back — then prices what is being left on the table: the ISK/hr you would add by tuning what is already built, and, as a separate figure, by rebuilding from scratch. Every rate is net of export customs and sales tax at your own Accounting level.

appraisal.question: What is this pile of loot actually worth?
appraisal.answer: Paste straight from your inventory, a multibuy or a fitting. The appraisal prices it at the trade hub you pick three ways — sold into buy orders now or listed one step under the cheapest seller, each net of the sales tax and broker fee that route pays, and reprocessed with your own skills. Copy a ready-made sell list, or share the result as a link.

notifications.desc: Per character, per event. Skills, industry jobs, extractors, calendar events and — with the corporation grant — structure fuel carry a timestamp, so those arrive with the app closed; order fills, mail, contracts and price alerts fire while it is open.

skills.name: Skills

industry.name: Industry
industry.desc: Build plans for manufacturing and reactions: materials, job fees, facility rigs and taxes at live hub prices. A production log tracks what each run really made, Opportunities ranks the blueprints you own and scans the market for what is profitable to build, and BPC Search covers every public blueprint-copy contract by ME/TE, runs, price and jumps.

miningTax.desc: Your output, ISK/hr and raw-vs-refined value over time, plus a tax ledger for moons you mine in someone else’s space: each day’s ore in each system assigned to the payee you owe, tax and ISK snapshotted at assignment, splits, settle-up and payment matching.

planetary.name: Planetary Industry
planetary.desc: Colonies, extraction timers and idle warnings, a chain planner that fits pins against CPU and powergrid, and an advisor that shows what each colony could earn by tuning or rebuilding it.

market.name: Market
market.desc: Order books for any region or all of them, filtered by jump range and security, with price history, side-by-side compare, price alerts, and an appraisal of pasted items or fits net of fees. Built on public price data, so it works whatever you did or didn't grant.

orders.name: Market Orders
orders.desc: Your open orders grouped by what is wrong with them, with the relist floor, the undercut that caused it, and the better exits — for every character at once.

walletOrders.name: Wallet & LP
walletOrders.desc: Balance, journal and transaction history, plus a loyalty store that ranks offers by what they are worth at your hub.

assets.name: Assets
assets.desc: Every hangar, station and structure your characters hold, searchable, with player structures resolved to real names.

contracts.name: Contracts
contracts.desc: Your contract history and what each one held, plus a search of public item exchange and courier contracts by jump range, with ISK per jump for couriers.

social.name: Mail & Calendar
social.desc: In-game mail with reply and forward, and a calendar you can RSVP from, without launching the client.

contacts.name: Contacts & Standings
contacts.desc: Contacts and the standings you set on them, for one character or across all of them at once, flagging where your characters disagree.

login.trustHeading: It reads. It writes only when you act.

readOnly.name: Four writes, and nothing else
readOnly.desc: Opening a mail flags it as read in EVE, answering a calendar invite sends your response, a reply or forward you write goes out through your account, and saving a Fitting to EVE recreates it on the game's side. Nothing else in the app writes to EVE.

token.name: Your refresh token stays in this browser
token.desc: It lives in this browser's own storage and nowhere else — never on a server, never in a log. Signing in to sync exchanges one short-lived access token and never the refresh token. Remove a character and it goes with it.

offline.name: Works when the connection doesn't
offline.desc: Install it like an app. It keeps serving what it last fetched when ESI is down or you have no signal, and syncs your own plans across your devices.

openSource.name: Free, and open to read
openSource.desc: No account to create, no ads, no subscription, no paid tier. Read the source before you decide to trust it.

faq.storeIntro: Neocom Desk keeps as little as possible on a server. The short version: we store the things you make in the app, and none of what we read from EVE on your behalf.

synced.title: Synced between your devices
synced.description: Saved so your work looks the same on your phone, your laptop and your desktop. Filed under each character’s EVE character ID — never a name, an email address, or an account we invented.
synced.skillPlans: Skill Plans — the plans you build. The skills you have actually trained come from EVE and stay on this device.
synced.buildPlans: Build Plans — the blueprint, runs, ME/TE, facility and hub you picked.
synced.productionRuns: Production Runs — what you logged as built, and the sales and orders you linked to it.
synced.quickbar: Your Quickbar — the items you saved in the Market browser.
synced.stationPins: The stations and structures you pinned in Assets.
synced.piPicks: The resources you chose to pull on each planet in the PI Advisor.
synced.fittings: The Fittings you saved to My Fittings: name and share code.
synced.miningTaxNote: The payees you named and the entries you assigned to them, including the ore and ISK figures snapshotted at that moment — that snapshot is the invoice, so it has to travel with it.
synced.notificationFeedNote: Ones you have already been shown, so another device can catch up on what it missed. Kept for 30 days.
synced.settings: The settings you chose on this page.
synced.settingsNote: Your notification preferences, the PI customs rates you overrode, your industry build groups, the defaults every page starts from — trade hub, industry facility, reaction facility, assumed ME and assumed TE, the PI expiring-soon window, the corp dark threshold, and the default characters shown — the appraisal price percentage you set on the Market page, whether SP Extraction monitoring is on along with the SP threshold you set for it, whether blueprint cost counts toward Industry profit, the ISK-per-LP value you set for LP Store blueprints, whether each character is Alpha or Omega, the ore types you tagged as moon ore or ignored on the Moon Mining Tax ledger's unclassified-ore banner, which skill plan you're adding skills to from Fit Check and Market, the fitting damage profiles you made along with which one fittings are measured against, and the fitting target profiles you made along with which one applied DPS is worked out against. Nothing else on this page leaves your device.

local.title: Kept on this device only
local.description: Everything Neocom Desk reads from EVE is cached in this browser and refetched from ESI when it goes stale. None of it is uploaded. Three things Neocom Desk writes back to your account: opening a mail here marks it read in EVE too, so it stays read after you reload; responding to a calendar invite here sends that response to EVE; and sending a reply or forward you compose in Mail sends that mail through your account. Nothing else — no orders, no colony changes, no mail you didn't write and send yourself — is ever written.
local.esi: Your assets, wallet, contracts, mail, contacts, clones, calendar, skills, skill queue, industry jobs and colonies.
local.corp: Everything on the Corporation pages — wallet, members, structures, assets and moon extractions.
local.market: Market prices, order books and the LP store.
local.miningHistory: Up to 90 days of your mining ledger, kept past the 30 days EVE itself returns so the Mining Overview can show longer ranges.
local.loginNote: The token that keeps you logged in is stored in this browser and nowhere else.
local.preferences: The rest of Settings — text size and time format, which answer for the screen you are looking at — and every sort, filter and expanded section a page remembers as you use it.

notes.push: Push notifications, if you turn them on: we store a token for this device, the character IDs it covers, and the alerts due in the next 72 hours — including their text, so they can be delivered while the app is closed. Each character is verified with EVE at that moment, and the token used for that check is discarded straight after.
notes.crashes: Crash reports: when something goes wrong we receive the error and which page it happened on, so it can be fixed. IP addresses are switched off, request and response bodies are never captured, and your EVE tokens are stripped before anything is sent.
notes.removal: Removing a character deletes everything above from our servers. If its EVE login has already expired we cannot sign in to do that, so the deletion runs the next time you add that character back.
notes.export: Exporting a backup (Data tab) writes a password-encrypted file — including your sign-in tokens — to your device. This only happens when you press the button, and the file goes wherever you choose to put it; we never see it.
